messages:
incident-bot: P1 alert: smart-routing health oscillation detected across regions for service: inference-api. Affected regions: us-east-1 <-> eu-west-1. Error spike: 502/504 and increased tail latency. Triggered at 2026-11-03T02:14Z (alert_id: SR-4471).
liam (oncall-sre): acked. paging liam -> /pager notify SRE oncall. i'm looking now. any customer-reported hits?
jack (cust-sre): a couple of enterprise customers reported timeouts and retries, one reported failover to a warm-disabled model variant. sending their request ids.
liam (oncall-sre): thanks. initial hypothesis: health-check thresholds too aggressive after the health-check tuning we rolled 2h ago, causing quick failover between regions. that triggers routing fallback, which then causes cross-region requests that in turn make the other region appear unhealthy -> loop.
anna? (typo fixed) anna (eng-runtime): i'm @anna, running a quick health check sweep. pulling routing logs and prefix cache metrics.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: noticed recent change: health-check-config v3.4.1 applied to regional pools at 2026-11-03T00:12Z by ci/cd (change-id: hc-3.4.1).
liam (oncall-sre): ok. can we temporarily disable cross-region fallback policy for this customer-facing pool? that should stop the flip-flop. command?
anna? anna (eng-runtime): command: "infractl routing set-policy --pool inference-api-prod --policy prefer-local --disable-cross-region-fallback". running a dry-run first.
liam (oncall-sre): do it. dry-run looks good. run live.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): executing now.
ops-bot: infractl: command accepted. policy updated for pool inference-api-prod: cross-region-fallback=disabled (applied by anna).
liam (oncall-sre): monitoring metrics. check 5xx rate and tail latency.
jack (cust-sre): customers seeing immediate reduction in retries. one customer reported 60% drop in error surface. :thumbsup:
maya (product): please note any impact to capacity - disabling fallback could increase load on primary region. we may need to enable burst capacity or let Dedicated pools absorb.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): noted. i'm scaling us-east pool by +10% capacity and enabling warm-burst for 15m as a safety valve. command: "infractl capacity adjust --pool us-east-1/inference-api --delta +10 --warm-burst 15m".
ops-bot: capacity API: adjustment accepted. scaling initiated.
liam (oncall-sre): visual checks: regional health oscillation graph shows stabilization after policy change and scaleup. tail latency trending down.
liam (oncall-sre): can someone grep routing logs for any older requests that selected wrong model variant during the loop? we saw mention of warm-disabled variant earlier. need to confirm scope of model-variant misrouting.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): grep show few requests that were routed to fallback-quant-1 (quantized variant) because of transient unhealthy tag. adding a short-term sticky rule to avoid switching model variants while fallback-disabled.
liam (oncall-sre): ok. apply sticky rule: 
```
infractl routing add-rule --pool inference-api-prod --rule "sticky_on_fail=true; stick_duration=300s; allowed_variants=[production, production-quant]"
```
anna? anna (eng-runtime): rule applied.
jack (cust-sre): documenting reported customer ids and sample request ids in the incident ticket 2026-11-03-4471. will reach out to affected customers with mitigation summary.
liam (oncall-sre): good. we should also rollback the health-check-config v3.4.1 to previous stable v3.3.8 after this stabilizes. not yet - let's watch for 15 minutes post-change.
ops-bot: alert: 5m post-change check - 5xx down 78%, p99 latency down 52% for inference-api-prod.
maya (product): what's the impact window to report? we'll need a customer-facing blurb.
jack (cust-sre): estimated affected window: 2026-11-03T00:12Z -> 2026-11-03T02:18Z (when cross-region fallback disabled) for incomplete requests and retries. some requests retried successfully; a subset saw 502s.
liam (oncall-sre): preparing a short incident summary for internal Slack and create an incident in the tracker. status -> mitigated (manual intervention). tagging eng-runtime for postmortem.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): noted. i'll collect logs, health-check diffs, and a timeline. also capturing config change history: hc-3.4.1 introduced decreased healthy_threshold from 5->2 and probe timeout 1s->500ms. that made health flip faster under moderate transient network.
liam (oncall-sre): that's the smoking gun. proposed follow-ups: 1) revert hc-3.4.1 and add canary with traffic shaping 2) add hysteresis to routing decisions to require sustained unhealthy for 45s before failover 3) enhance observability: per-region failover counter and alert on >3 flips in 10m.
maya (product): agree, also we need a customer comms draft. jack, can you own?
jack (cust-sre): will draft and send to legal/comms in 30m.
liam (oncall-sre): handing off to anna for deep dive and postmortem. i'm going offline for sleep window. anna, you're primary. please escalate to oncall-sre-2 if you need immediate help.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): taking over. i've captured required artifacts and started a deep-dive runbook. will open postmortem and link timelines, config diffs, affected customers, and mitigation commands.
liam (oncall-sre): one last note: we applied temporary mitigations (disabled cross-region fallback, sticky rules, +10% capacity) — i'll mark incident as resolved in tracker after 1h of stable metrics.
ops-bot: incident-bot: incident SR-4471 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned to anna (eng-runtime) for postmortem.
anna? anna (eng-runtime): ack. starting postmortem doc skeleton and will ping infra/security if any config audit required.
liam (oncall-sre): thanks team. great coordination. :raised_hands:
